'''David Hamilton Koch''' ({{IPAc-en|k|oʊ|k}} {{respell|KOHK}}; May 3, 1940&nbsp;– August 23, 2019) was an American businessman, philanthropist, limited government advocate and [[chemical engineer]]. In 1970, he joined the family business: [[Koch Industries]], the second-largest privately held company in the United States. He became president of the subsidiary Koch Engineering in 1979 and became a co-owner of Koch Industries (along with elder brother [[Charles Koch|Charles]]) in 1983. Koch served as an executive vice president of Koch Industries until he retired due to health issues in 2018.

Koch was a [[Libertarianism in the United States|libertarian]]. He was the 1980 [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] candidate for Vice President of the United States and helped finance the campaign. He founded [[Citizens for a Sound Economy]] and donated to advocacy groups and [[Political activities of the Koch brothers|political campaigns]], the majority of which were [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]]. Koch became a Republican in 1984; in 2012, he spent over $100&nbsp;million in a failed bid to oppose the re-election of President [[Barack Obama]].

As of 2012, Koch was the fourth-richest person in the United States, and as of 2013 the wealthiest resident of [[New York City]]. As of June 2019, Koch was ranked as the [[List of richest people|11th-richest person in the world]] (tied with his brother Charles), with a [[net worth]] of $50.5&nbsp;billion. Koch contributed to the [[Lincoln Center]], [[Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center|Sloan Kettering]], [[NewYork–Presbyterian Hospital]], and the Dinosaur Wing at the [[American Museum of Natural History]]. The New York State Theater at Lincoln Center, home of the [[New York City Ballet]], was renamed the [[David H. Koch Theater]] in 2008 following Koch's gift of $100&nbsp;million for the renovation of the theater.

== Early life and education ==
Koch was born in [[Wichita, Kansas]], the son of Mary Clementine (née Robinson) and [[Fred C. Koch|Fred Chase Koch]], a chemical engineer. David's paternal grandfather, [[Harry Koch (businessman)|Harry Koch]], was a Dutch immigrant who founded the ''Quanah Tribune-Chief'' newspaper and was a founding shareholder of the [[Quanah, Acme and Pacific Railway]].<ref name="new netherland">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nnp.org/nni/Publications/Dutch-American/kochd.htm |title=Koch, David Hamilton (1940) |publisher=New Netherland Project |access-date=August 31, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100819225843/http://www.nnp.org/nni/Publications/Dutch-American/kochd.htm |archive-date=August 19, 2010 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> David was the third of four sons, with elder brothers [[Frederick R. Koch|Frederick]], [[Charles Koch|Charles]], and nineteen-minute-younger twin<ref name="kochbtp" /> [[Bill Koch (businessman)|Bill]]. His maternal ancestors included [[William Ingraham Kip]], an Episcopal bishop; and [[Elizabeth Clementine Stedman]], a writer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.palmbeachdailynews.com/obituaries/20190824/palm-beach-obituary-bill-koch-remembers-brother-david-as-rsquooutstanding-human-best-friendrsquo|title=Palm Beach obituary: Bill Koch remembers brother David as 'outstanding human, best friend'|first=Shannon|last=Donnelly|website=Palm Beach Daily News|access-date=November 25, 2019|archive-date=September 14, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190914104342/https://www.palmbeachdailynews.com/obituaries/20190824/palm-beach-obituary-bill-koch-remembers-brother-david-as-rsquooutstanding-human-best-friendrsquo|url-status=live}}</ref>

Koch attended the [[Deerfield Academy]] prep school in Massachusetts, graduating in 1959. He attended [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT), earning both a [[bachelor's degree|bachelor's]] (1962) and a master's degree (1963) in [[chemical engineering]]. He was a member of the [[Beta Theta Pi]] fraternity. Koch played basketball at MIT, averaging 21 points per game at MIT over three years, a school record. He also held the single-game scoring record of 41 points from 1962 until 2009, when it was eclipsed by [[Jimmy Bartolotta]].<ref name="kochbtp">{{Cite magazine |url=https://newrepublic.com/article/114135/david-and-william-koch-mit-basketball-players |title=David and William Koch as MIT Basketball Players |magazine=The New Republic |date=August 14, 2013 |access-date=June 10, 2015 |archive-date=January 26, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180126070735/https://newrepublic.com/article/114135/david-and-william-koch-mit-basketball-players |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Role at Koch Industries ==
In 1970, Koch joined [[Koch Industries]] under his brother [[Charles Koch|Charles]], to work as a technical-services manager. He founded the company's New York City office and in 1979 he became the president of his own division, Koch Engineering, renamed Chemical Technology Group. David's brothers [[Frederick R. Koch|Frederick]] and [[Bill Koch (businessman)|Bill]] had inherited stock in Koch Industries. In June 1983, after a bitter legal and boardroom battle, the stakes of Frederick and Bill were bought out for $1.1&nbsp;billion and Charles Koch and David Koch became majority owners in the company.<ref>{{Cite news | url= https://www.nytimes.com/1998/04/28/business/brother-versus-brother-koch-family-s-long-legal-feud-is-headed-for-a-jury.html | title=Brother Versus Brother; Koch Family's Long Legal Feud Is Headed for a Jury | first=Leslie | last= Wayne | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=April 28, 1998 | url-status=live | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180326160300/https://www.nytimes.com/1998/04/28/business/brother-versus-brother-koch-family-s-long-legal-feud-is-headed-for-a-jury.html | archive-date=March 26, 2018 | df=mdy-all}}</ref><ref name=MorningSun>"Koch's wife granted order of restraint". Pittsburg (KS) ''Morning Sun'', July 21, 2000.</ref> Legal disputes against Charles and David lasted roughly two decades. Frederick and Bill sided with [[J. Howard Marshall III]], [[J. Howard Marshall II]]'s eldest son, against Charles and David at one point, in order to take over the company. In 2001, Bill reached a settlement in a lawsuit where he had charged the company was taking oil from federal and Indian land; that settlement ended all litigation between the brothers.<ref name=WallStreet>"Judge Clears Koch Brothers' Settlement Pact". ''Wall Street Journal'', May 29, 2001.</ref> [[CBS News]] reported that Koch Industries settled for $25&nbsp;million.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/blood-and-oil/ |title=Blood And Oil |work=CBS News |date=November 27, 2000 |access-date=October 15, 2015 |archive-date=April 23, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110423143904/http://www.cbsnews.com/stories/2000/11/27/60II/main252545.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

As of 2010, David Koch owned 42 percent of Koch Industries, as did his brother Charles.<ref name=Wallet /> He held four U.S. patents.<ref name="TimeObit">{{Cite magazine |url=https://time.com/5660040/david-koch-legacy/ |title=David Koch's Millions Remade the Republican Party. He Didn't Like the Results |magazine=Time |date=August 23, 2019 |first=Philip |last=Elliott |access-date=August 23, 2019 |archive-date=August 23, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190823192633/https://time.com/5660040/david-koch-legacy/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Koch served as an executive vice president of Koch Industries until retiring due to health issues in 2018.<ref name="asgbio">{{cite web |url=http://www.theadvocates.org/celebrities/david-koch.html |title= Advocates for Self-Government - Libertarian Education|website=www.theadvocates.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070226111813/http://www.theadvocates.org/celebrities/david-koch.html |archive-date=February 26, 2007}}</ref> His retirement was announced on June 5, 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/powerpost/wp/2018/06/05/david-koch-is-leaving-koch-industries-stepping-down-from-americans-for-prosperity/ |title=David Koch is leaving Koch Industries, stepping down from Americans for Prosperity |first=James |last=Hohmann |date=June 5, 2018 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=June 5, 2018 |archive-date=June 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180605135809/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/powerpost/wp/2018/06/05/david-koch-is-leaving-koch-industries-stepping-down-from-americans-for-prosperity/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Political involvement ==
{{See also|Political activities of the Koch brothers}}

===Campaigns===
[[File:David Koch 1980.jpg|thumb|150px|Koch in 1980]]
Koch was the [[United States Libertarian Party|Libertarian Party]]'s vice-presidential candidate in the [[1980 United States presidential election|1980 presidential election]],<ref>{{Cite news |title=Man Without a Candidate |author-link=Charlotte Curtis |first=Charlotte |last=Curtis |date=October 16, 1984 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/10/16/arts/man-without-a-candidate.html |access-date=July 18, 2015 |archive-date=July 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150723112247/http://www.nytimes.com/1984/10/16/arts/man-without-a-candidate.html |url-status=live }}</ref> sharing the party ticket with presidential candidate [[Ed Clark]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bennett |first=James T. |title=Not Invited to the Party: How the Demopublicans Have Rigged the System and Left Independents Out in the Cold |date=October 3, 2009 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-1-4419-0365-5 |location=New York |pages=167 |language=en}}</ref> The Clark–Koch [[Ticket (election)|ticket]] proposed downsizing the government through the elimination of various federal laws and departments. These included abolishing [[Social Security (United States)|Social Security]], the [[Federal Reserve Board]], [[welfare spending|welfare]], [[minimum-wage]] laws, corporate taxes, all price supports and subsidies for agriculture and business, and [[U.S. Federal agencies]] including the SEC, EPA, ICC, FTC, OSHA, FBI, CIA, and DOE.<ref name="Mayer" /><ref name=Buck>Rinker Buck, [https://books.google.com/books?id=ueUCAAAAMBAJ&dq=David+Koch&pg=PA22 "How Those Libertarians Pay the Bills"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140619144039/http://books.google.com/books?id=ueUCAAAAMBAJ&lpg=PA18&dq=David%20Koch&pg=PA22#v=onepage&q=David%20Koch&f=false |date=June 19, 2014 }}, [[New York (magazine)|''New York'' magazine]], November 3, 1980</ref> Their platform proposed privatizing all transportation and inland waterways. The ticket received 921,128 votes, 1% of the total nationwide vote.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/national.php?year=1980&off=0&f=1|title=1980 Presidential General Election Results|first=David|last=Leip|publisher=uselectionatlas.org|access-date=August 31, 2010|archive-date=June 5, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605021346/http://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/national.php?year=1980&off=0&f=1|url-status=live}}</ref> This was the Libertarian Party national ticket's best showing until [[2016 United States presidential election|2016]] in terms of percentage and its best showing in terms of raw votes until the [[2012 United States presidential election|2012 presidential election]], although that number was surpassed again in 2016.<ref name=Bennett>James T. Bennett, [https://books.google.com/books?id=eImBSPX63D0C&dq=ed+clark+highest+vote+total+1980&pg=PA167 ''Not Invited to the Party: How the Demopublicans Have Rigged the System and Left Independents Out in the Cold''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140620072236/http://books.google.com/books?id=eImBSPX63D0C&pg=PA167&dq=ed+clark+highest+vote+total+1980&hl=en&ei=YZB9TMd3goHyBufjrZkH&sa=X&oi=book_result&ct=result&resnum=3&ved=0CDcQ6AEwAg#v=onepage&q=ed%20clark%20highest%20vote%20total%201980&f=false |date=June 20, 2014 }}, Springer, 2009, p. 167, {{ISBN|1-4419-0365-8}}.</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Quixotic '80 Campaign Gave Birth to Kochs' Powerful Network |author-link=Nicholas Confessore |first=Nicholas |last=Confessore |date=May 17, 2014 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/05/18/us/politics/quixotic-80-campaign-gave-birth-to-kochs-powerful-network.html |access-date=July 18, 2015 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |archive-date=June 14, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150614043840/http://www.nytimes.com/2014/05/18/us/politics/quixotic-80-campaign-gave-birth-to-kochs-powerful-network.html |url-status=live }}</ref> "Compared to what [the Libertarians had] gotten before," Charles said, "and where we were as a movement or as a political/ideological point of view, that was pretty remarkable, to get 1 percent of the vote."<ref name=Continetti>{{Cite news|first=Matthew|last=Continetti|author-link=Matthew Continetti|title=The Paranoid Style in Liberal Politics|work=[[The Weekly Standard]]|date=April 4, 2011|url=https://www.weeklystandard.com/matthew-continetti/the-paranoid-style-in-liberal-politics |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180420133442/https://www.weeklystandard.com/matthew-continetti/the-paranoid-style-in-liberal-politics |archive-date=April 20, 2018}}</ref>

After the bid, according to journalist [[Brian Doherty (journalist)|Brian Doherty]]'s ''[[Radicals for Capitalism]]'', Koch viewed politicians as "actors playing out a script".<ref name=Mayer /><ref name="Doherty2008">{{Cite book|last=Doherty|first=Brian|author-link=Brian Doherty (journalist)|title=Radicals for Capitalism: A Freewheeling History of the Modern American Libertarian Movement|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6g_NGAAACAAJ|access-date=October 10, 2011|date=May 26, 2008|publisher=Perseus Books Group|isbn=978-1-58648-572-6|page=410}}{{Dead link|date=January 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Koch credited the 1976 presidential campaign of [[Roger MacBride]] as his inspiration for getting involved in politics:

<blockquote style=font-size:100%>Here was a great guy, advocating all the things I believed in. He wanted less government and taxes, and was talking about repealing all these victimless crime laws that accumulated on the books. I have friends who smoke pot. I know many homosexuals. It's ridiculous to treat them as criminals&nbsp;— and here was someone running for president, saying just that.<ref name=Buck /></blockquote>

Koch gave his own vice presidential campaign $100,000 a month after being chosen as [[Ed Clark]]'s running mate. "We'd like to abolish the [[Federal Election Commission]] and all the limits on campaign spending anyway," Koch said in 1980. When asked why he ran, he replied: "Lord knows I didn't need a job, but I believe in what the Libertarians are saying. I suppose if they hadn't come along, I could have been a big Republican from [[Wichita, Kansas|Wichita]]. But hell&nbsp;— ''everybody'' from Kansas is a Republican."<ref name=Buck />

In 1984, Koch broke with the Libertarian Party when it supported eliminating all taxes; in a letter to [[David Bergland]], the Libertarian candidate for the 1984 presidential election, Koch referred to Bergland's platform as "extreme", predicting that the country would be thrown into "utter chaos" if it was implemented. Subsequently, Koch shifted the bulk of his financial support to [[Republican Party (United States)|the Republican Party]], though he continued to contribute to several Libertarian campaigns in local races.<ref name=Wallet />{{Rp|4}} Koch donated to various [[Political activities of the Koch brothers|political campaigns]], most of which were [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.opensecrets.org/orgs/summary.php?id=D000000186&cycle=A |title=Koch Industries: Summary |publisher=OpenSecrets.org |access-date=June 10, 2015 |archive-date=September 5, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905234531/https://www.opensecrets.org/orgs/summary.php?id=D000000186&cycle=A |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = https://kochdocs.org/2019/06/07/david-koch-most-radical-extreme-positions-viable-clark-koch-platform/|title = 1983-1984 David Koch: The "Most Radical and Extreme Positions" Viable Are from the Clark/Koch 1980 Platform|date = June 7, 2019|access-date = May 1, 2021|archive-date = May 1, 2021|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210501234236/https://kochdocs.org/2019/06/07/david-koch-most-radical-extreme-positions-viable-clark-koch-platform/|url-status = live}}</ref> In February 2012, during the [[Wisconsin gubernatorial recall election]], Koch said of Wisconsin governor [[Scott Walker (politician)|Scott Walker]], "We're helping him, as we should. We've gotten pretty good at this over the years. We've spent a lot of money in Wisconsin. We're going to spend more," and said that by "we" he meant Americans for Prosperity.<ref>{{Cite news |title=David Koch intends to cure cancer in his lifetime and remake American politics |date=February 20, 2012 |access-date=May 29, 2015 |newspaper=[[The Palm Beach Post]] |url=http://www.palmbeachpost.com/news/business/david-koch-intends-to-cure-cancer-in-his-lifetime-/nL4Fb/ |first=Stacey |last=Singer |archive-date=June 10, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120610155539/http://www.palmbeachpost.com/news/business/david-koch-intends-to-cure-cancer-in-his-lifetime-/nL4Fb/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Billionaire Koch brothers gave $8&nbsp;million to Wisconsin Gov. Scott Walker recall campaign, Dem chair says |first=Tom |last=Kertscher |date=June 20, 2012 |access-date=May 29, 2015 |url=http://www.politifact.com/wisconsin/statements/2012/jun/20/debbie-wasserman-schultz/billionaire-koch-brothers-gave-8-million-wisconsin/ |publisher=[[PolitiFact]] |archive-date=June 3, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150603092515/http://www.politifact.com/wisconsin/statements/2012/jun/20/debbie-wasserman-schultz/billionaire-koch-brothers-gave-8-million-wisconsin/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=On Politics: David Koch: 'We've spent a lot of money in Wisconsin. We're going to spend more.' |date=February 20, 2012 |access-date=May 29, 2015 |first=Mary |last=Spicuzza |newspaper=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |url=http://host.madison.com/news/local/govt-and-politics/on-politics/on-politics-david-koch-we-ve-spent-a-lot-of/article_dc909fe4-5bde-11e1-a0db-0019bb2963f4.html |archive-date=October 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001185816/https://madison.com/news/local/govt-and-politics/on-politics/on-politics-david-koch-we-ve-spent-a-lot-of/article_dc909fe4-5bde-11e1-a0db-0019bb2963f4.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2012, Koch spent over $100&nbsp;million in a failed bid to oppose the re-election of President [[Barack Obama]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/11/15/us/politics/122-million-in-2012-spending-by-koch-group.html |title=$122 Million in 2012 Spending by Koch Group |last=Confessore |first=Nicholas |date=November 14, 2013 |work=The New York Times |access-date=August 25, 2019 |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=August 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190825061958/https://www.nytimes.com/2013/11/15/us/politics/122-million-in-2012-spending-by-koch-group.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/tariniparti/billionaire-david-koch-dies |title=Billionaire David Koch, Who Shaped Modern Conservative Politics, Has Died |access-date=August 25, 2019 |publisher=[[BuzzFeed News]] |archive-date=August 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190825061958/https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/tariniparti/billionaire-david-koch-dies |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Views ===
{{Libertarianism US|activists}}
Koch supported policies that promoted [[Libertarian conservatism|smaller government]] and lower taxes.<ref name="kochnyt">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/03/05/us/05koch.html|date=March 5, 2011|work=The New York Times|title=Cancer Research Before Activism, Billionaire Conservative Donor Says|last=Cooper|first=Michael|access-date=February 7, 2017|archive-date=January 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170116074234/http://www.nytimes.com/2011/03/05/us/05koch.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>The Koch Brothers December 24, 2012, p. 96 Forbes</ref>  He was against the [[Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act]] and the Dodd–Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act.<ref name="Wallet" /><ref name="kochnyt" /> Koch said he wasn't sure if [[global warming]] was  anthropogenic, and thought a warmer planet would be "good", with lengthened growing seasons mitigating problems caused by disappearing coastlines and mass migrations. "Earth will be able to support enormously more people, because a far greater land area will be available to produce food".<ref name="Wallet" /><ref name="kochnyt" /> Koch opposed the [[Iraq War]], saying that the war has "cost a lot of money and it's taken so many American lives", and "I question whether that was the right thing to do. In hindsight that looks like it was not a good policy."<ref name=Continetti /> In an impromptu interview with the blog ThinkProgress, he was quoted as saying he would like the new, 2011 Republican Congress to "cut the hell out of spending, balance the budget, reduce regulations, and support business".<ref name="kochtp">{{Cite news |url=http://thinkprogress.org/politics/2011/01/06/137586/koch-teaparty-us/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130903032310/http://thinkprogress.org/politics/2011/01/06/137586/koch-teaparty-us/|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 3, 2013|publisher=ThinkProgress|date=January 6, 2011|last=Fang |first=Lee|title=Exclusive: Polluter Billionaire David Koch Says Tea Party 'Rank And File Are Just Normal People Like Us'}}</ref> Koch considered himself a [[Cultural liberalism|social liberal]]<ref name="Bell">{{Cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/blogs/politics/2014/12/billionaire-david-koch-says-hes-a-social-liberal/|title=Billionaire David Koch Says He's a Social Liberal|work=ABC News|date=December 14, 2014|access-date=December 29, 2014|first=Benjamin|last=Bell|archive-date=December 26, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141226175715/http://abcnews.go.com/blogs/politics/2014/12/billionaire-david-koch-says-hes-a-social-liberal/|url-status=live}}</ref> who supported women's [[right to choose]],<ref name="Fischer">{{Cite news |url=http://www.cnn.com/2014/12/14/politics/david-koch-gay-rights-abortion-democrats/ |title=David Koch is pro-choice, supports gay rights; just not Democrats |work=CNN|date=December 15, 2014 |access-date=December 29, 2014 |first=Sara |last=Fischer |archive-date=December 29, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141229203306/http://www.cnn.com/2014/12/14/politics/david-koch-gay-rights-abortion-democrats/ |url-status=live }}</ref> [[LGBT rights in the United States|gay rights]], [[same-sex marriage]], and [[stem-cell research]].<ref name="Wallet" /><ref>Joseph Patrick McCormick, [http://www.pinknews.co.uk/2012/09/02/billionaire-gop-supporter-disagrees-with-platform-says-he-supports-gay-marriage/ Billionaire GOP supporter disagrees with platform, says he supports gay marriage] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141102102131/http://www.pinknews.co.uk/2012/09/02/billionaire-gop-supporter-disagrees-with-platform-says-he-supports-gay-marriage/ |date=November 2, 2014 }}, ''[[PinkNews]]'', September 2, 2012</ref> He opposed the [[war on drugs]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Coaston |first1=Jane |title="David Koch walked the walk": a libertarian on the Koch brother's legacy |url=https://www.vox.com/2019/8/23/20829962/david-koch-libertarian-legacy |date=August 23, 2019 |work=Vox |access-date=August 28, 2019 |archive-date=August 26, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190826134724/https://www.vox.com/2019/8/23/20829962/david-koch-libertarian-legacy |url-status=live }}</ref>

Koch opposed several of President [[Barack Obama]]'s policies. An article from the ''[[Weekly Standard]]'', detailing the "left's obsession" with the Koch brothers, quotes Koch stating that Obama is "the most radical president we've ever had as a nation ... and has done more damage to the free enterprise system and long-term prosperity than any president we've ever had".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.weeklystandard.com/articles/paranoid-style-liberal-politics_555525.html?nopager=1|title=The Paranoid Style in Liberal Politics|work=[[The Weekly Standard]]|access-date=April 14, 2011|archive-date=April 15, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110415091748/https://www.weeklystandard.com/articles/paranoid-style-liberal-politics_555525.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Koch said that Obama's father's economic [[socialism]], practiced in [[Kenya]], explains why Obama has "sort of antibusiness and anti-free enterprise" influences.<ref name=Continetti /> Koch said that Obama is "scary", a "hardcore socialist" who is "marvelous at pretending to be something other than that".<ref name="Intel">{{Cite news|url=https://nymag.com/daily/intel/2011/05/billionaire_conservative_david.html|title=David Koch Gives President Obama Zero Credit for Bin Laden's Death|work=New York|first=Sarah|last=Owen|date=May 5, 2011|access-date=February 18, 2020|archive-date=October 21, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121021232659/http://nymag.com/daily/intel/2011/05/billionaire_conservative_david.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Koch contributed almost entirely to Republican candidates in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2012/11/charts-map-koch-brothers-2012-spending|title=Charts: How Much Have the Kochs Spent on the 2012 Election?|work=Mother Jones|access-date=July 9, 2018|archive-date=June 29, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180629234530/https://www.motherjones.com/politics/2012/11/charts-map-koch-brothers-2012-spending/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Advocacy ===
Koch donated funds to various advocacy groups.<ref name="Wallet" /> In 1984, he founded [[Citizens for a Sound Economy]] (CSE).<ref name=Mazur>Suzan Mazur, [https://books.google.com/books?id=wk2FfQQ_DmsC&pg=PA244 "The Altenberg 16: An Exposé of the Evolution Industry"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611043228/https://books.google.com/books?id=wk2FfQQ_DmsC&pg=PA244 |date=June 11, 2020 }}, ''North Atlantic Books'', 2010, 343 pages</ref> He served as its chairman of the board of directors and donated funds to it. [[Richard H. Fink]] served as its first president.<ref name=Continetti /> Koch was the chairman of the board and gave initial funding to the [[Americans for Prosperity|Americans for Prosperity Foundation]] and to a related advocacy organization, [[Americans for Prosperity]]. A Koch Industries spokesperson issued a press release stating "No funding has been provided by Koch companies, the Koch foundations, or Charles Koch or David Koch specifically to support the tea parties."<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2010/08/30/covert-operations|title=Covert Operations|first=Jane|last=Mayer|date=August 30, 2010|magazine=The New Yorker|access-date=November 25, 2019|archive-date=July 28, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140728193318/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2010/08/30/covert-operations|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="WeigelFW">{{Cite news |url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/right-now/2010/04/dick_armey_please_koch_keep_di.html |first=David |last=Weigel |title=Dick Armey: Please, Koch, keep distancing yourself from me |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=April 15, 2010 |access-date=September 27, 2010 |archive-date=September 10, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210910162528/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/right-now/2010/04/dick_armey_please_koch_keep_di.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Koch was the top initial funder of the Americans for Prosperity Foundation at $850,000.<ref>{{Cite news |title=David Koch Seeded Major Tea-Party Group, Private Donor List Reveals |first=Alex |last=Seitz-Wald |date=September 24, 2013 |access-date=March 20, 2015 |url=http://www.nationaljournal.com/politics/david-koch-seeded-major-tea-party-group-private-donor-list-reveals-20130924 |work=[[National Journal]] |quote=But a donor list filed with the IRS labeled "not open for public inspection" from 2003, the year of AFP's first filing, lists David Koch as by far the single largest contributor to its foundation, donating $850,000. |archive-date=March 17, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150317094948/http://www.nationaljournal.com/politics/david-koch-seeded-major-tea-party-group-private-donor-list-reveals-20130924 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Money in Politics: The Companies Behind David Koch's Americans For Prosperity |first=Pema |last=Levy |date=September 24, 2013 |access-date=March 20, 2015 |url=http://www.ibtimes.com/money-politics-companies-behind-david-kochs-americans-prosperity-1410408 |work=[[International Business Times]] |quote=David Koch was the top contributor, providing $850,000. |archive-date=April 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402144352/http://www.ibtimes.com/money-politics-companies-behind-david-kochs-americans-prosperity-1410408 |url-status=live }}</ref> Koch said that he sympathized with the [[Tea Party movement]], but denied directly supporting it, having stated that: "I've never been to a tea party event. No one representing the tea party has ever even approached me."<ref name=Wallet />

Koch sat on the board of the libertarian [[Cato Institute]] and [[Reason Foundation]] and donated to both organizations.<ref name="Mayer">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.newyorker.com/reporting/2010/08/30/100830fa_fact_mayer |title=Covert Operations: The billionaire brothers who are waging a war against Obama |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |date=August 30, 2010 |first=Jane |last=Mayer |author-link=Jane Mayer |access-date=February 18, 2020 |archive-date=October 7, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007183130/http://www.newyorker.com/reporting/2010/08/30/100830fa_fact_mayer |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=Wallet /><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB125064719500442047 |title=Conservatives Take a Page From Left's Online Playbook |journal=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=August 20, 2009 |first=Jake |last=Sherman |url-access=subscription |access-date=August 3, 2017 |archive-date=January 30, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170130050904/http://www.wsj.com/articles/SB125064719500442047 |url-status=live }}</ref> The Koch brothers have been involved in blocking regulations and legislation to confront climate change since 1991, when the Cato Institute held the "Global Environmental Crisis: Science or Politics?"<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Mayer |first1=Jane |title="Kochland" Examines the Koch Brothers' Early, Crucial Role in Climate-Change Denial |url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/daily-comment/kochland-examines-how-the-koch-brothers-made-their-fortune-and-the-influence-it-bought |magazine=The New Yorker |date=August 13, 2019 |access-date=May 9, 2020 |archive-date=August 29, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190829093101/https://www.newyorker.com/news/daily-comment/kochland-examines-how-the-koch-brothers-made-their-fortune-and-the-influence-it-bought |url-status=live }}</ref> According to ''NPR'', the Koch brothers gave "over $145 million to climate-change denying think tanks and advocacy groups between 1997 and 2018."<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.npr.org/2021/10/27/1047583610/once-again-the-u-s-has-failed-to-take-sweeping-climate-action-heres-why | title=How decades of disinformation about fossil fuels halted U.S. Climate policy | work=NPR }}</ref>

In August 2010, [[Jane Mayer]] wrote an article in ''[[The New Yorker]]'' on the political spending of David and Charles Koch. It stated: "As their fortunes grew, Charles and David Koch became the primary underwriters of hard-line libertarian politics in America."<ref name="Mayer" /> An opinion piece by journalist [[Yasha Levine]] in ''[[The New York Observer]]'' said Mayer's article had failed to mention that the Kochs' "free market philanthropy belies the immense profit they have made from [[corporate welfare]]".<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://observer.com/2010/09/7-ways-the-koch-bros-benefit-from-corporate-welfare/ |last=Levine |first=Yasha |author-link=Yasha Levine |date=September 1, 2010 |title=7 Ways the Koch Bros. Benefit from Corporate Welfare |work=[[The New York Observer]] |access-date=December 30, 2014 |archive-date=December 31, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231071732/http://observer.com/2010/09/7-ways-the-koch-bros-benefit-from-corporate-welfare/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2011, 2014, and 2015 ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine included Charles and David Koch among the [[Time 100|''Time'' 100]] of the year, for their involvement in supporting the [[Tea Party movement]] and the criticism they received.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Ferguson|first=Andrew|title=The 2011 TIME 100|url=http://www.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,2066367_2066369_2066324,00.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110425093926/http://www.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,2066367_2066369_2066324,00.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 25, 2011|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|access-date=April 22, 2011 |date=April 21, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title='Their own media megaphone': what do the Koch brothers want from Time? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2017/nov/27/koch-brothers-time-magazine-media-power |work=The Guardian |date=November 27, 2017 |first=Lucia |last=Graves|access-date=May 9, 2020 |archive-date=May 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200511141935/https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2017/nov/27/koch-brothers-time-magazine-media-power |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Prison reform ====
In July 2015, David and Charles Koch were commended by both President Obama and activist [[Van Jones|Anthony Van Jones]] for their bipartisan efforts to reform the prison system in the United States.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Nelson|first=Colleen Mccain | last2=Fields | first2=Gary|title=Obama, Koch Brothers in Unlikely Alliance to Overhaul Criminal Justice|work=The Wall Street Journal|date=July 16, 2015|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/obama-koch-brothers-in-unlikely-alliance-to-overhaul-criminal-justice-1437090737|url-access=subscription|access-date=March 6, 2017|archive-date=February 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170216192938/https://www.wsj.com/articles/obama-koch-brothers-in-unlikely-alliance-to-overhaul-criminal-justice-1437090737|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=wapos>{{Cite news|last=Horwitz|first=Sari|title=Unlikely Allies|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=August 15, 2015|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sf/national/2015/08/15/clemency-the-issue-that-obama-and-the-koch-brothers-actually-agree-on/|access-date=August 26, 2017|archive-date=September 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170913044313/http://www.washingtonpost.com/sf/national/2015/08/15/clemency-the-issue-that-obama-and-the-koch-brothers-actually-agree-on/|url-status=live}}</ref> For nearly 10 years, the Kochs advocated for several reforms within the criminal justice system which include reducing recidivism rates, simplifying the employment process for the rehabilitated, and defending private property from government seizures through [[asset forfeiture]].<ref name=wapos /><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://cjonline.com/news/2015-10-15/forfeiture-reform-aligns-likes-billionaire-charles-koch-aclu |title=Forfeiture reform aligns likes of billionaire Charles Koch, ACLU |work=[[The Topeka Capital-Journal]] |date=October 15, 2015 |first=Mary |last=Hudetz |access-date=November 13, 2015 |archive-date=January 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114205427/http://cjonline.com/news/2015-10-15/forfeiture-reform-aligns-likes-billionaire-charles-koch-aclu |url-status=live }}</ref> Allying with groups such as the [[ACLU]], the [[Center for American Progress]], [[Families Against Mandatory Minimums]], the [[Coalition for Public Safety]], and the [[John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation|MacArthur Foundation]], the Kochs maintained that current prison system unfairly targeted low-income and minority communities at the expense of the public budget.<ref name=wapos />

The Koch brothers' advocacy has also attracted scrutiny and criticism. Michelle Chen, writing in ''The Nation'', and William C. Anderson, writing in ''The Guardian'', caution that the Kochs' efforts reflect broader interests in further privatizing the criminal justice system.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chen |first=Michelle |date=2018-03-16 |title=Beware of Big Philanthropy’s New Enthusiasm for Criminal Justice Reform |url=https://www.thenation.com/article/archive/beware-of-big-philanthropys-new-enthusiasm-for-criminal-justice-reform/ |access-date=2025-06-05 |work=The Nation |language=en-US |issn=0027-8378}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2015/jul/17/prison-industrial-complex-big-business-koch-brothers | title=Big business built the prison state. Why should we trust them to tear it down? | newspaper=The Guardian | date=July 17, 2015 | last1=Anderson | first1=William C. }}</ref> In 2015, ''The Intercept'' reported that the Kochs' philanthropic efforts exist alongside continued funding of "tough-on-crime" political candidates and committees pushing for harsher sentencing.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://theintercept.com/2015/11/03/soft-on-crime-ads/ | title=Koch Brothers Talk Criminal Justice Reform, but Pay for "Tough on Crime" Political Ads | date=November 3, 2015 }}</ref> Writing in ''Political Research Associates'', Kay Whitlock argues that the Kochs' avid support for measures such as [[mens rea]] or "criminal intent" reform exemplify "an agenda of deregulation and relief for 'overcriminalized' corporations and executives" rather than concern for individual rights of the accused.<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://politicalresearch.org/2017/06/06/endgame-how-bipartisan-criminal-justice-reform-institutionalizes-a-right-wing-neoliberal-agenda | title=Endgame | journal=Political Research Associates | date=June 6, 2017 | last1=Whitlock | first1=Kay }}</ref>

== Philanthropy ==
Koch established the [[Koch family foundations#David H. Koch Charitable Foundation|David H. Koch Charitable Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web|publisher=Koch Family Foundations|url=http://www.kochfamilyfoundations.org/FoundationsDHK.asp|title=David H. Koch Charitable Foundation and Personal Philanthropy|access-date=November 17, 2014|archive-date=November 9, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141109170430/http://www.kochfamilyfoundations.org/FoundationsDHK.asp|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Levinthal|first1=Dan|title=The Koch brothers' foundation network explained|url=https://www.publicintegrity.org/2015/10/30/18713/koch-brothers-foundation-network-explained|publisher=The Center for Public Integrity|access-date=April 12, 2018|date=October 30, 2015|archive-date=April 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413043509/https://www.publicintegrity.org/2015/10/30/18713/koch-brothers-foundation-network-explained|url-status=live}}</ref> Beginning in 2006, the ''[[Chronicle of Philanthropy]]'' listed Koch as one of the world's top 50 philanthropists.<ref name=autogenerated1>{{Cite web|title=No. 45: David H. Koch |url=http://philanthropy.com/section/Philanthropy-50/370/ |publisher=The Chronicle of Philanthropy |access-date=October 8, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111008194753/http://philanthropy.com/section/Philanthropy-50/370 |archive-date=October 8, 2011}}</ref> He sat on the Board of Trustees of [[NewYork–Presbyterian Hospital]] from 1988 until his death in 2019.<ref name=NYP>{{Cite web|title=Hospital Leadership - Board of Trustees|url=http://nyp.org/about/board-trustees.html|publisher=New York Presbyterian|access-date=July 7, 2019|archive-date=January 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160128171451/http://nyp.org/about/board-trustees.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Overall, Koch donated more than $1.3 billion to [[Philanthropy|philanthropic causes]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Block |first=Fang |title=David Koch's Philanthropic Legacy |url=https://www.barrons.com/articles/david-kochs-philanthropic-legacy-01566596839 |access-date=November 29, 2023 |website=[[Barron's]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Arts ===
Koch had a lifelong interest in the arts, which he attributed to his mother's role in introducing him to opera and ballet during his childhood.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/08/23/arts/david-koch-arts-patron.html|title=David Koch, Embraced as an Arts Patron, Even as Criticism Grew|first1=Elizabeth A.|last1=Harris|first2=Robin|last2=Pogrebin|newspaper=The New York Times|date=August 23, 2019|access-date=October 24, 2019|archive-date=October 24, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191024030044/https://www.nytimes.com/2019/08/23/arts/david-koch-arts-patron.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In July 2008, Koch pledged $100&nbsp;million over 10 years to renovate the New York State Theater in the [[Lincoln Center|Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts]]; the Theater is the home of the New York City Ballet.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/07/10/arts/10linc.html |title=David H. Koch to Give 100 Million to Theater |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=July 10, 2008 |first=Robin |last=Pogrebin |access-date=February 7, 2017 |archive-date=April 21, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421043258/http://www.nytimes.com/2008/07/10/arts/10linc.html |url-status=live }}</ref> According to ''The New York Times'', Koch's gift was "transformative, enabling a full-scale renovation of the stage" that included "an enlarged orchestra pit that mechanically rises". The theater was renamed the [[David H. Koch Theater]].<ref name=":0" /> Koch also pledged $10&nbsp;million to renovate fountains outside the [[Metropolitan Museum of Art]].<ref name=Souccar>{{Cite news |url=http://www.crainsnewyork.com/article/20100627/ANNIVERSARY/100619869/1072 |title=It's a Philanthropy Thing |work=Crain's New York Business |date=June 27, 2010 |first=Miriam Kreinin |last=Souccar |access-date=September 27, 2010 |archive-date=July 3, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100703045015/http://www.crainsnewyork.com/article/20100627/ANNIVERSARY/100619869/1072 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was elected to the Board of Trustees of The Metropolitan Museum of Art in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|title=David H. Koch Elected a Trustee at The Metropolitan Museum of Art|url=https://www.metmuseum.org/press/news/2008/david-h-koch-elected-a-trustee-at-the-metropolitan-museum-of-art|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200930033039/https://www.metmuseum.org/press/news/2008/david-h-koch-elected-a-trustee-at-the-metropolitan-museum-of-art|archive-date=September 30, 2020|access-date=January 16, 2022|website=www.metmuseum.org|date=November 12, 2008 }}</ref>

Koch was the longest-serving trustee of the [[American Ballet Theatre]],<ref name=":0"/> serving on its board for 25 years<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.palmbeachdailynews.com/society/insider/american-ballet-theatre-celebrates-70th-season-david-kochs-723608.html |title=American Ballet Theatre Celebrates 70th Season, David Koch's Birthday |work=[[Palm Beach Daily News]] |date=June 2, 2010 |first=Shannon |last=Donnelly |access-date=September 27, 2010 |archive-date=June 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100610070256/http://www.palmbeachdailynews.com/society/insider/american-ballet-theatre-celebrates-70th-season-david-kochs-723608.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and contributing more than $6&nbsp;million to the theater.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2010-05-17/david-koch-toasted-by-michelle-obama-caroline-kennedy-at-n-y-ballet-gala.html |title=David Koch Toasted by Caroline Kennedy, Robert DeNiro |publisher=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=May 17, 2010 |first=Patrick |last=Cole |access-date=March 6, 2017 |archive-date=April 28, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140428104510/http://www.bloomberg.com/news/2010-05-17/david-koch-toasted-by-michelle-obama-caroline-kennedy-at-n-y-ballet-gala.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He was also a member of the Board of Trustees of [[WGBH-TV]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.wgbh.org/about/BoardofTrustees.cfm |title=Board of Trustees |publisher=WGBH |access-date=June 10, 2015 |archive-date=June 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623075255/http://www.wgbh.org/about/BoardofTrustees.cfm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last1=Cohan|first1=William|title=David Koch's Chilling Effect on Public Television|newspaper=Bloomberg.com|date=June 10, 2013|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/view/articles/2013-06-09/david-koch-s-chilling-effect-on-public-television|publisher=Bloomberg|access-date=April 12, 2018|archive-date=October 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181006075418/https://www.bloomberg.com/view/articles/2013-06-09/david-koch-s-chilling-effect-on-public-television|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Education ===
From 1982 to 2013, Koch contributed $18.6&nbsp;million to [[WGBH Educational Foundation]], including $10&nbsp;million to the [[Public Broadcasting Service]] (PBS) show ''[[Nova (American TV program)|Nova]]''.<ref name="heraldwgbhkoch">{{Cite news |url=http://www.bostonherald.com/news_opinion/local_coverage/2013/10/activists_put_heat_on_gbh_to_oust_donor_board_giant |date=October 4, 2013 |work=[[Boston Herald]] |last=Cassidy |first=Chris |title=Activists put heat on 'GBH to oust donor, board giant |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141208052702/http://www.bostonherald.com/news_opinion/local_coverage/2013/10/activists_put_heat_on_gbh_to_oust_donor_board_giant |archive-date=December 8, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/funders/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181010185627/http://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/about/funders.html |url-status=live |date=October 10, 2018 |archive-date=October 10, 2018 |access-date=October 17, 2018 |title=Funders |publisher=[[WGBH-TV]] |quote=Funders for Season 44 include Draper, 23andMe, Cancer Treatment Centers of America, the David H. Koch Fund for Science, the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, and PBS Stations. ... Funders for Season 40 include Boeing (episodes 4007, 4009-4015, 4017-4024), Lockheed Martin (episodes 4003-4005) Franklin Templeton (episodes 4007, 4009-4016) the David H. Koch Fund for Science, the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, and PBS Stations.}}</ref> Koch was a contributor to the [[Smithsonian Institution]] in Washington, D.C., including a $20&nbsp;million gift to the [[American Museum of Natural History]] (AMNH), creating the David H. Koch Dinosaur Wing and a contribution of $15&nbsp;million to the [[National Museum of Natural History]] to create the new ''[[David H. Koch Hall of Human Origins]]'', which opened on the museum's 100th anniversary of its location on the National Mall on March 17, 2010.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/gallery/2010/03/17/GA2010031702837.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100325031817/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/gallery/2010/03/17/GA2010031702837.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 25, 2010 |title=Smithsonian to Open Hall Dedicated to Story of Human Evolution |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=March 30, 2010 }}</ref> Koch served on the advisory council for the Smithsonian<ref name=":0" /> and the board of the AMNH.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Yuhas |first=Alan |date=January 21, 2016 |title=David Koch steps down from board of New York science museum |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2016/jan/21/david-koch-american-museum-of-natural-history-climate-change-fossil-fuel-money |access-date=November 29, 2023 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He also served on the executive board of the [[Institute of Human Origins]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=IHO Research Council and Executive Board|url=https://iho.asu.edu/people/iho-research-council |publisher=Institute of Human Origins|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160419193708/https://iho.asu.edu/people/iho-research-council|archive-date=April 19, 2016}}</ref> In 2012, Koch contributed US$35&nbsp;million to the [[Smithsonian]] to build a new dinosaur exhibition hall at the [[National Museum of Natural History]].<ref name=dino$>{{Cite web |url=http://newsdesk.si.edu/releases/smithsonian-s-national-museum-natural-history-build-new-dinosaur-hall |title=Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History to Build New Dinosaur Hall &#124; Newsdesk |publisher=Newsdesk.si.edu |date=May 3, 2012 |access-date=June 10, 2015 |archive-date=July 21, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721195936/http://newsdesk.si.edu/releases/smithsonian-s-national-museum-natural-history-build-new-dinosaur-hall |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=David Koch donates $35&nbsp;million to National Museum of Natural History for dinosaur hall|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/style/david-koch-donates-35-million-to-national-museum-of-natural-history-for-dinosaur-hall/2012/05/03/gIQAIjT3yT_story.html|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=May 3, 2012|access-date=January 24, 2016|issn=0190-8286|first=Jacqueline|last=Trescott|archive-date=July 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170719171853/https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/style/david-koch-donates-35-million-to-national-museum-of-natural-history-for-dinosaur-hall/2012/05/03/gIQAIjT3yT_story.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Koch was also a benefactor of the [[Deerfield Academy]], his alma mater. The academy's natatorium, science center, and field house are named after him.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.recorder.com/DA-alum-David-Koch-dies-27936537|title=DA alum David Koch dies|date=August 24, 2019|website=Greenfield Recorder|access-date=November 25, 2019|archive-date=September 13, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190913222640/https://www.recorder.com/DA-alum-David-Koch-dies-27936537|url-status=live}}</ref> Koch was named the academy's first Lifetime Trustee.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2010/08/30/covert-operations|title=The Koch Brothers' Covert Ops|first=Jane|last=Mayer|magazine=The New Yorker |date=August 23, 2010|via=www.newyorker.com|access-date=November 25, 2019|archive-date=July 28, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140728193318/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2010/08/30/covert-operations|url-status=live}}</ref> He contributed $70 million to the boarding school.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=David Koch Named Lifetime Trustee|url=https://deerfieldscroll.net/2010/02/david-koch-named-lifetime-trustee/|website=The Deerfield Scroll|date=2010-02-25|access-date=2025-11-29|language=en-US|last=parkjongwon.com}}</ref>

=== Medical research ===
Koch said his biggest contributions go toward a "moon shot" campaign to finding the cure for cancer, according to his profile on [[Forbes]].<ref name="forbes" /> Between 1998 and 2012, Koch contributed at least $395&nbsp;million to medical research causes and institutions.<ref name=PhilMag>{{Cite news|last=Sparks|first=Evan|title=The Team Builder|url=http://www.philanthropyroundtable.org/topic/excellence_in_philanthropy/the_team_builder|access-date=September 26, 2012|newspaper=[[Philanthropy (magazine)|Philanthropy]]|date=Summer 2012|archive-date=February 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150215050048/http://www.philanthropyroundtable.org/topic/excellence_in_philanthropy/the_team_builder|url-status=live}}</ref>

Koch has sat on the Board of Trustees of [[NewYork–Presbyterian Hospital]] since 1987.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nyp.org/about-us/governance-and-leadership/board-of-trustees|title=NYP.org About Us Governance and Leadership Board of Trustees|access-date=July 7, 2019|archive-date=August 11, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811131036/https://www.nyp.org/about-us/governance-and-leadership/board-of-trustees|url-status=live}}</ref>  In 2007 he donated $15&nbsp;million to NewYork–Presbyterian.<ref name="WSJ 20071009">{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB119189124817352914|title=Institutional Gift, With a Catch|first=Sally|last=Beatty|date=October 9, 2007|work=[[The Wall Street Journal]]|url-access=subscription|access-date=August 3, 2017|archive-date=April 12, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180412212210/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB119189124817352914|url-status=live}}</ref>  In 2013, he gave $100&nbsp;million to NewYork–Presbyterian Hospital, the then-largest philanthropic donation in its history, beginning a $2&nbsp;billion campaign, to conclude in 2019, for a new [[ambulatory care]] center and renovation of the infrastructure of the hospital's five sites.<ref name=NYPresb>{{Cite web|last=NewYork-Presbyterian|title=NewYork-Presbyterian Announces $100 Million Donation from David H. Koch – Largest in Hospital's History – to Fund Outpatient Facility on Manhattan's East Side|url=http://nyp.org/news/hospital/David-Koch-Donation-2013.html|access-date=June 1, 2013|date=April 2, 2013|archive-date=September 19, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200919152851/https://www.nyp.org/news/hospital/David-Koch-Donation-2013.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Koch was a member of the board of directors of the Prostate Cancer Foundation and contributed $41&nbsp;million to the foundation, including $5&nbsp;million to a collaborative project in the field of [[nanotechnology]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.pcf.org/site/c.leJRIROrEpH/b.5801629/k.8E55/David_H_Koch_8211_Prostate_Cancer_Foundation_NanoMedicine_Gift_Announced.htm |title=David H. Koch – Prostate Cancer Foundation Nano-Medicine Gift Announced |publisher=PCF.org |date=October 12, 2007 |access-date=June 10, 2015 |archive-date=May 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150502090404/http://www.pcf.org/site/c.leJRIROrEpH/b.5801629/k.8E55/David_H_Koch_8211_Prostate_Cancer_Foundation_NanoMedicine_Gift_Announced.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Dolan|first1=Kerry|title=Warren Buffett Has Plenty of Company Among Powerful in Battling Prostate Cancer|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/kerryadolan/2012/04/17/warren-buffett-has-plenty-of-company-among-prostate-cancer-survivors/#66538e462c78|work=Forbes|access-date=April 12, 2018|archive-date=April 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413044442/https://www.forbes.com/sites/kerryadolan/2012/04/17/warren-buffett-has-plenty-of-company-among-prostate-cancer-survivors/#66538e462c78|url-status=live}}</ref> An eponym of the David H. Koch Chair of the Prostate Cancer Foundation, the position is held by [[Dr. Jonathan Simons]].<ref>{{Cite press release|title=Clinical Data for World's First Truly Non-Invasive Prostate Cancer Test Published in JAMA Oncology|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20160412005315/en/Clinical-Data-World%E2%80%99s-Non-Invasive-Prostate-Cancer-Test|publisher=Exosome Diagnostics|access-date=April 12, 2018|date=April 12, 2016|archive-date=April 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180413124803/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20160412005315/en/Clinical-Data-World%E2%80%99s-Non-Invasive-Prostate-Cancer-Test|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2006, Koch gave $20&nbsp;million to [[Johns Hopkins University]] [[Johns Hopkins School of Medicine|School of Medicine]] in [[Baltimore]] for cancer research. The building he financed was named the David H. Koch Cancer Research Building.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/news/media/releases/david_koch_gives_20_million_for_hopkins_cancer_research|title=David Koch Gives $20 Million for Hopkins Cancer Research|publisher=hopkinsmedicine.org|access-date=September 27, 2010|archive-date=August 31, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100831113950/http://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/news/media/releases/david_koch_gives_20_million_for_hopkins_cancer_research|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2007, he contributed $100&nbsp;million to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology for the construction of a new {{Convert|350000|sqft|m2|adj=on}} research and technology facility to serve as the home of the [[David H. Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.kochfamilyfoundations.org/pdfs/Koch%2002-2008%20%20Spectrum%20EmpathyforOthers.pdf |title=Empathy For Others |publisher=Kochfamilyfoundations.org |access-date=June 10, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120311202401/http://www.kochfamilyfoundations.org/pdfs/Koch%2002-2008%20%20Spectrum%20EmpathyforOthers.pdf |archive-date=March 11, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> From the time he joined the MIT Corporation in 1988, Koch has given at least $185&nbsp;million to MIT,<ref name=PhilMag /> and $30&nbsp;million to the [[Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center]] in New York City.<ref name="WSJ 20071009" /> The same year, he donated $25&nbsp;million to the [[University of Texas M. D. Anderson Cancer Center]] in [[Houston]] to establish the David Koch Center for Applied Research in Genitourinary Cancers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chron.com/news/houston-texas/article/Koch-gives-18-million-gift-to-M-D-Anderson-1800063.php|title=Koch gives $18 million gift to M.D. Anderson|date=November 10, 2007|website=Houston Chronicle|access-date=December 4, 2019|archive-date=December 4, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191204144601/https://www.chron.com/news/houston-texas/article/Koch-gives-18-million-gift-to-M-D-Anderson-1800063.php|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2011 Koch gave $5&nbsp;million to the House Ear Institute, in Los Angeles, to create a center for hearing restoration,<ref name=autogenerated1 /> and $25&nbsp;million to the [[Hospital for Special Surgery]] in New York City<ref>{{Cite web|title=No. 45: David H. Koch|url=http://philanthropy.com/article/No-45-David-H-Koch/126132/|publisher=The Chronicle of Philanthropy|access-date=October 8, 2011|archive-date=March 19, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110319025007/http://philanthropy.com/article/No-45-David-H-Koch/126132/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.joshfriedland.com/pdfs/HSS_DtoR_13_Fall_2007.pdf |title=Discovery to Recovery : Clinical and Research Highlights at HSS |date=2007 |publisher=Joshfriedland.com |access-date=June 10, 2015 |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303194239/http://www.joshfriedland.com/pdfs/HSS_DtoR_13_Fall_2007.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2015, he committed $150&nbsp;million to [[Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center]] in New York City to build the David H. Koch Center for Cancer Care,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morrell |first=Alex |title=Billionaire David Koch Pledges Record $150 Million For New Cancer Center |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexmorrell/2015/05/20/billionaire-david-koch-pledges-record-150-million-for-new-cancer-center/ |access-date=September 4, 2022 |website=Forbes |language=en |archive-date=September 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220904010334/https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexmorrell/2015/05/20/billionaire-david-koch-pledges-record-150-million-for-new-cancer-center/ |url-status=live }}</ref> which will be housed in a 23-story building in development between East 73rd and 74th Streets overlooking the [[FDR Drive]]. The center will combine state-of-the-art cancer treatment in an environment that supports patients, families, and caregivers. The building will include flexible personal and community spaces, educational offerings, and opportunities for physical exercise.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mskcc.org/press-releases/msk-receives-gift-150-million-david-koch-patient-facility|title=Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center Receives Record Gift of $150&nbsp;million from David Koch for Innovative Patient Care Facility|access-date=May 20, 2015|date=May 20, 2015|archive-date=July 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150723025815/https://www.mskcc.org/press-releases/msk-receives-gift-150-million-david-koch-patient-facility|url-status=live}}</ref> Koch also donated $10&nbsp;million to the [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]] for [[Mathematical and theoretical biology|biomathematics]] research.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Department |first=Communications |date=November 9, 2006 |title=CSHL Raises $2.5 Million at Inaugural Double Helix Medals Event & Launches $200 Million Capital Campaign |url=https://www.cshl.edu/cshl-raises-25-million-at-inaugural-double-helix-medals-event-a-launches-200-million-capital-campaign/ |access-date=September 4, 2022 |website=Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory |language=en-US |archive-date=September 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220904010336/https://www.cshl.edu/cshl-raises-25-million-at-inaugural-double-helix-medals-event-a-launches-200-million-capital-campaign/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Heath-Harris |first=Rochelle |date=February 21, 2022 |title=A Billionaire's Affairs: David Koch |url=https://www.citysignal.com/a-billionaires-affairs-david-koch/ |access-date=September 4, 2022 |website=CitySignal |language=en-US |archive-date=September 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220904010337/https://www.citysignal.com/a-billionaires-affairs-david-koch/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Wealth ==
Koch was the fourth-richest person in the United States in 2012 and was the wealthiest resident of New York City in 2013.<ref name="forbes">{{Cite news|agency=Forbes|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/david-koch|title=David Koch – Forbes|date=March 9, 2011|access-date=June 10, 2015|archive-date=June 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623005858/http://www.forbes.com/profile/david-koch/|url-status=live}}</ref> As of June 2019, Koch was ranked as the 11th-richest person in the world (tied with his brother Charles), with a fortune of $50.5&nbsp;billion.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/david-koch/ |title=David Koch |website=[[Forbes]] |access-date=June 2, 2019 |archive-date=October 20, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171020073912/https://www.forbes.com/profile/david-koch/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
[[File:Fred with David and Julia Koch (1518448020).jpg|thumb|[[Fred Thompson]] poses with David Koch and his wife [[Julia Koch]].]]
In February 1991, Koch was seriously injured as a passenger on board [[Los Angeles runway disaster|USAir Flight 1493]] when it collided with another aircraft on a runway at [[Los Angeles International Airport]], killing 35 people.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1991/03/07/opinion/last-in-line-for-the-exit.html|title=Last in Line for the Exit|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 7, 1991|access-date=August 23, 2019|archive-date=August 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190823164927/https://www.nytimes.com/1991/03/07/opinion/last-in-line-for-the-exit.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Koch survived and said in an interview in 2014 that it helped change his life and prompted him to become "tremendously philanthropic."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/video/david-koch-plane-crash-helped-change-life-27598921|title=David Koch on the Plane Crash That Helped Change His Life|work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|date=December 15, 2014|access-date=August 23, 2019|archive-date=August 23, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190823181128/https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/video/david-koch-plane-crash-helped-change-life-27598921|url-status=live}}</ref>

When he was named lifetime trustee at Deerfield Academy in 2010, he said: “I would like to be known in the future as someone who is not just a wealthy, successful businessman but someone who really cared about the well-being of others—did his darndest to be charitable and help others.”<ref name=":1" />

Following [[Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis]]' death in 1994, Koch purchased her 15-room apartment at [[1040 Fifth Avenue]]. In 1996 he married [[Julia Flesher]].<ref name="Woman Ascending">{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/01/11/magazine/woman-ascending-a-marble-staircase.html?pagewanted=all |title=Woman Ascending A Marble Staircase |first=Elizabeth |last=Bumiller |work=The New York Times |date=January 11, 1998 |access-date=August 31, 2010 |archive-date=May 13, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100513230703/http://www.nytimes.com/1998/01/11/magazine/woman-ascending-a-marble-staircase.html?pagewanted=all |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="weddings">{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/05/26/style/weddings-julia-m-flesher-david-h-koch.html |title=Weddings: Julia M. Flesher, David H. Koch |work=The New York Times |date=May 26, 1996 |access-date=September 2, 2010 |archive-date=December 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211224081448/https://www.nytimes.com/1996/05/26/style/weddings-julia-m-flesher-david-h-koch.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The apartment "wasn't roomy enough" after the birth of their third child, so Koch sold it to billionaire [[Glenn Dubin]] in 2006 and moved with his family to [[740 Park Avenue]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 26, 2006 |title=Jackie Flat Gets $32 M. |url=https://observer.com/2006/06/jackie-flat-gets-32-m-2/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190826051101/https://observer.com/2006/06/jackie-flat-gets-32-m-2/ |archive-date=August 26, 2019 |access-date=August 26, 2019 |website=[[The New York Observer]]|first= Michael|last=Calderone}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Goldman|first= Leah |title=Check Out The 18 Most Expensive Hedge Fund Homes In America. |work=Business Insider|date= November 5, 2010 |access-date=May 16, 2020|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/most-expensive-hedge-fund-homes-2010-11}}</ref> They had three children together; David Jr., Mary Julia, and John.<ref name="McFadden">{{Cite news |last1=McFadden |first1=Robert D. |title=David Koch, Billionaire Who Fueled Right-Wing Movement, Dies at 79 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/08/23/us/david-koch-dead.html |access-date=August 24, 2019 |work=The New York Times |date=August 23, 2019 |archive-date=August 24, 2019 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20190824141827/https://www.nytimes.com/2019/08/23/us/david-koch-dead.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Mary Julia is an associate opinion editor at [[The Wall Street Journal]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Opinion {{!}} My Journal Preserved My Dad’s Last Days|url=https://www.wsj.com/opinion/my-journal-preserved-my-dads-last-days-9060b0d7|website=The Wall Street Journal|date=2025-10-22|access-date=2025-11-29|language=en-US|first=Mary Julia|last=Koch}}</ref> and formerly was a staff reporter for ''[[The New York Sun]]''<ref>{{Cite web |title=M.J. Koch |url=https://www.nysun.com/author/m-j-koch |access-date=November 29, 2023 |website=The New York Sun |language=en}}</ref> and editor-in-chief of ''[[The Harvard Independent]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mary Julia Koch, Author at Harvard Independent |url=https://harvardindependent.com/author/maryjuliakoch/ |access-date=November 29, 2023 |website=Harvard Independent |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Health and death===
In 1992, Koch was diagnosed with [[prostate cancer]]. He underwent radiation, surgery, and hormone therapy, but the cancer repeatedly returned. Koch said he believed his experience with cancer encouraged him to fund medical research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://heavy.com/news/2019/08/david-koch-cause-of-death-cancer/|title=David Koch's Cause of Death: 5 Fast Facts You Need to Know|first=Alyssa|last=Choiniere|date=August 24, 2019|access-date=November 25, 2019|archive-date=August 24, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190824074748/https://heavy.com/news/2019/08/david-koch-cause-of-death-cancer/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Koch died at his home in [[Southampton, New York]], on August 23, 2019, at the age of 79.<ref name = McFadden/> Koch's wife, [[Julia Koch]], and their three children inherited a 42% stake in Koch Industries from Koch upon his death.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/julia-koch/?list=forbes-400#2fab53562b9c|title=Julia Koch & family|website=[[Forbes]]|access-date=October 22, 2019|archive-date=December 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191230072122/https://www.forbes.com/profile/julia-koch/?list=forbes-400#2fab53562b9c|url-status=live}}</ref>
